title: 6 Fruits and Vegetables Loaded With Pesticides - Consumer Reports
summary: Consumer Reports analysis of USDA residue data naming six conventional crops with high pesticide risk and recommending organic or lower-risk swaps.

assertions.quote: While close to two-thirds of these foods are ranked low or very low risk, pesticides pose a serious problem in conventionally grown versions

verdicts.note: Risk-weighted analyses of USDA residue data find a small set of crops, mostly with organophosphate or carbamate residues, account for most dietary pesticide risk.
Residues are concentrated: over 95% of Dirty Dozen samples had residues versus about 40% of Clean Fifteen samples, but this is residue frequency, not risk.

EWG's claim that avoiding the Dirty Dozen cuts pesticide intake by four-fifths had no exposure quantification behind it, and modelled exposure from those crops was already orders of magnitude below effect levels, so buying them organic gives no appreciable risk reduction.

EFSA found that around 75% of the highest acute exposures in children were driven by a single substance in a specific commodity, mostly samples over the legal limit; it shows concentration in particular commodity-pesticide pairs, not that buying a few crops organic removes most risk.

assertions.quote: organic blueberries pose very low risks
Samples of bell peppers have consistently been among the highest-risk produce in every year they have been tested
Even imported organic green beans were very high-risk, the only organic food with that rating.
